subject: Dup-guard: defer to judge instead of rejecting (admit provisional + enqueue)
description:
Turn the note-write near-duplicate guard from a hard REJECT into a DEFER-TO-JUDGE. Today routes/overlay.js:369-401 rejects any note whose title-vec cosine >= DUP_THRESHOLD (0.70) against a current note, returning {ok:false,duplicate:true,match,hint}; the caller (often a small worker model) must then skip / supersede / force. Two bad outcomes: a genuinely-distinct note gets silently DROPPED (skip), or the guard gets NEUTERED (reflexive force:true). The dumb write path should not decide duplicate-vs-distinct; the intelligent dup-judge should.

DESIGN (admit-provisional, reuse existing dup-cluster judge pipeline):
1. On guard fire (cosine>=0.70, no supersedes/force): ADMIT the note via addNoteNode but flag it pending_dup so it is RETRIEVAL-INVISIBLE (excluded from RAG/search recall, like weight-0 edges / the provisional flag already in the codebase). Record the match key. Enqueue a dup-cluster judgment for {new, match} via markEagerJudge(newNoteKey) so the next judge pass surfaces the pair through dupClusters() (the same pipeline that already handles 0.55-0.70 stragglers).
2. Return {ok:true, pending_dup:true, note_key, match} so the caller just moves on — no skip/supersede/force burden.
3. Judge verdict (existing dup-cluster adjudication): CONSOLIDATE (merge into match, supersede the new) / DISTINCT (clear pending_dup -> note becomes recall-eligible) / SUPERSEDE (new replaces match). Only the verdict stamps judgedAtEpoch and clears provisional.
4. TIMEOUT FALLBACK (mirror judging->ready exactly): if the judge has not run within judgingTimeoutMs, flip pending_dup (invisible) -> provisional (visible) as a PURE DERIVED classification (like judgingState), so the note is usable and never permanently buried. CRITICAL: timeout must be NON-DESTRUCTIVE — do NOT clear the eager mark / judging anchor / queue membership on timeout. Clearing them is the forbidden failure mode (item drops from queue, never re-judged). The item stays enqueued+unstamped (judgedAtEpoch < epoch) so the dup-judge STILL adjudicates it after the timeout; only an actual verdict stamps it judged + clears provisional. Lifecycle: pending_dup(invisible,queued) -> [judge] verdict, OR -> [timeout] provisional(visible,STILL queued) -> [judge] verdict. Never lost, never permanently unadjudicated.
5. Keep force:true as the explicit bypass for a certain caller. Optional cheap fast-path: at very-high cosine (>=0.90 near-certain clone) may still hard-reject or auto-consolidate without bothering the judge — implementer's call.

Touch points: routes/overlay.js (the guard block ~369-401), lib/overlay.js (addNoteNode pending_dup flag + provisional derivation + EMPTY/save persistence), lib/judge.js (dupClusters / eagerJudge surfacing of pending_dup pairs; ensure timed-out pending_dup stays queued), routes/judge.js (dup-cluster verdict handler clears pending_dup on DISTINCT, stamps judged), and the search/recall path that must EXCLUDE retrieval-invisible pending_dup notes. Add tests: guard-fire admits provisional+invisible+enqueued; DISTINCT verdict makes it visible; CONSOLIDATE supersedes; timeout flips visible WITHOUT clearing the queue mark and it is still re-judged; force:true bypasses.

summary: Turned the note-write dup guard from REJECT into DEFER-TO-JUDGE. On a guard fire (title-vec cosine >= 0.70, no supersedes/force) the note is now ADMITTED provisional via overlay.pendingDup{noteKey->{match,score,at}} (retrieval-invisible) and the {new,match} pair is enqueued for the dup-judge; response is {ok:true, pending_dup:true, note_key, match}. supersedes/force still bypass. Recall (/search) excludes invisible pending_dup notes (dupInvisible). Verdicts clear provisional: consolidate (supersede new into match / new replaces match) clears keep+superseded; markDistinct (DISTINCT) clears keys -> recall-eligible. NON-DESTRUCTIVE timeout: judge.pendingDupState mirrors judgingState EXACTLY (timedOut=now-at>=timeoutMs) flipping invisible->visible as a PURE derivation while NEVER mutating/dropping the entry, so a timed-out note stays queued + re-judgeable (judge.pendingDupClusters still surfaces it). pendingDup persists via EMPTY()/LOCAL_FIELDS. No >=0.90 fast-path added (kept surgical). Decision recorded re: queue-source vs eagerJudge (eagerJudge is edge-based, no-ops for the 0.70-0.80 band). Tests: new test/pending-dup.test.js 5/5; note-dup-guard.test.js updated to new contract (2/2, semantic leg skipped when embed sidecar cold); regression judge-queue 67, judge-verdict 32, judge-eager 19, judge-pressure 28, judge-neighborhood 22, overlay-split 32, costflow 34, autowire-note 16 all pass. judge-journal's 11 fails are pre-existing on main (edge-clf shadow-verdict), unrelated.
